Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called the "reservoir," which processes the input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically fixed, and only the output weights are trained. Reservoirs in ESNs are often trained using random connectivity to ensure they have a rich and diverse set of responses to the input signals.
